answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must bind identities through a stake-slashing prism that decomposes behavior into verifiable trust vectors. Agents commit cryptographic collateral where duplicate claims incur superlinear cost scaling: registering n identities requires burning stake proportional to O(n^2), rendering hollow clone swarms economically nonviable. Each identity's reputation functions like an indelible pigment, permanently locking slashed value upon deviation.
